summary.summary: Powys's Q4 report to 31 March 2026 shows total borrowing down £5.61m over the year to £362.03m even after £25m of new PWLB in Q4, with the CFR closing at £453.34m — £22.7m below the original estimate because capital schemes were reprofiled and extra Welsh Government grants landed. Financing costs came in at 3.8% of net revenue against 4.0% planned, but the report is explicit that the deferred borrowing 'will still be required in the future': the CFR is forecast to reach £614.20m by March 2028. The council was an active short-term lender to other authorities (£35.32m across six loans in Q4, all repaid by March 2026). Aged sundry debt rose £3.0m in the quarter to £15.51m, 73% of the over-three-month debt being hard-to-collect social care charges; all treasury prudential indicators were complied with.

signals.headline: Total borrowing fell £5.61m in 2025/26 to £362.03m at 31 March 2026 despite £25m of new PWLB in Q4; financing costs 3.8% of net revenue (£13.94m) vs 4.0% in the approved strategy
signals.why: A year of modest deleveraging with capital financing costs inside plan, helped by reprofiling and additional Welsh Government grants.

signals.headline: CFR forecast to rise from £453.34m at 31 March 2026 to £516.13m by March 2027 and £614.20m by March 2028 (+£161m in two years); the report states deferred borrowing 'will still be required in the future'
signals.why: This year's saving is a deferral, not an avoidance — the capital programme implies substantial new external borrowing at forecast PWLB rates above 5%.

news_drafts.headline: Powys puts 2027/28 budget gap at £10.0m, up £0.3m since February, and £51.8m over five years
news_drafts.lead:
Powys County Council's cabinet, meeting on 20 October 2026, was given an updated medium-term financial strategy that puts the indicative budget gap for 2027/28 at £10.0m. In February 2026 the gap was projected at £9.7m. The paper reports the gap rising after pressures were revised.

The strategy's table sets out the gap for each year to 2031/32: £10.029m in 2027/28, £14.898m in 2028/29, £12.864m in 2029/30, £5.763m in 2030/31 and £8.219m in 2031/32. Added together, the council's modelling gives a cumulative gap of £51.8m over the five years. The paper says this follows from its assumption for the Welsh Government settlement. For 2027/28 the table shows contract and other pressures of £14.075m and additional funding of £3.911m.

The paper says the council's Senior Leadership Team is reviewing service proposals. It also says actions under Sustainable Powys, the council's savings programme, are "not likely" to bridge the £10.0m gap alone. The council's quarter 1 strategic risk register, run on 27 July 2026, records the action to revise the medium-term financial strategy as completed. It says "to bridge the gap savings from the Sustainable Powys regime will ensure we can deliver a balanced financial plan".

news_drafts.headline: Powys budget gap for 2027/28 put at £10.0m, up £0.3m since February; £51.8m over five years
news_drafts.lead:
Powys County Council's plan for 2027/28 shows a gap of £10.0m between the £404.5m it expects to need to spend and the £394.5m it expects to receive, according to a Cabinet report on its medium-term financial strategy (its financial plan for the next three to five years) that the Finance Panel considers on 15 October. In February 2026 the gap was projected at £9.7m. The report says the gap has grown even though services have identified cost reductions.

The strategy's annual gaps are £10.0m in 2027/28, £14.9m in 2028/29, £12.9m in 2029/30, £5.8m in 2030/31 and £8.2m in 2031/32. Together they come to £51.8m over five years, once assumed rises in council tax and the government settlement are counted. The council is pursuing a transformation programme called "Sustainable Powys" to deliver efficiencies and cost reductions. The Finance Panel is asked to examine whether it is delivering the savings required and to monitor the actions to close the gap.

The report also covers schools. Budgets ratified by every governing body show schools together heading for a cumulative net deficit of £5.8m by 31 March 2029. Schools received £5.6m of additional funding for 2026/27, including support for pay awards, and are projected to draw £0.2m from their reserves this year. School reserves held at schools' own discretion moved from a surplus of £8.9m in 2021/22 to a deficit of £3.1m in 2025/26. The council says it is working with schools in deficit to bring their budgets back into balance.

news_drafts.headline: Growing Mid Wales Board faces delivery risks across £110m investment portfolio
news_drafts.lead: Six of seven major projects in Powys's £110 million Growing Mid Wales capital investment programme have been rated Amber on delivery confidence by formal gateway reviews, indicating material risks that require active management. The board's governance statement identifies financial profiling and funding drawdown — the pace and timing of capital deployment — as principal risks to the portfolio. A small number of projects required intervention to review delivery assumptions and refine financial profiles. The governance framework for the £110 million programme is undergoing its first full year of formal financial reporting, with Audit Wales scheduled to undertake external audit engagement in early 2027 following threshold changes and the move to full Statement of Accounts.

findings.headline: £22.4 million of grants included in Appendix D, of which £14.1 million are additional to the approved budget
findings.detail: The paper includes £8.3 million of grants expected within the approved budget and £14.1 million of additional grants, which are a mixture of new awards and amendments. Major grants include £2.1 million Local Growth Fund and £2.9 million Regional Integrated Fund.
findings.matters: A large share of the budget reliant on additional grant funding is a source of income that finance directors and lenders would weigh against its continuity.
findings.figures: Total grants £22,426,559; already in budget £8,299,603; additional £14,126,956; Local Growth Fund £2,108,347; Regional Integrated Fund £2,933,629
findings.quote: £14.1 million are additional and are included within this report to comply with financial

findings.headline: The 2026-27 pay award of 3.3% exceeds the 3% budgeted, a 0.3 percentage point pressure met from the risk budget
findings.detail: The paper requests a virement of £460,360 from the risk budget to fund the difference. Corporate Activities records the same 0.3 percentage point pressure within its forecast.
findings.matters: A pay award above budget, funded from a central risk budget, is a cost pressure that peer councils with similar award settlements will face.
findings.figures: Pay award 3.3% against 3% budgeted; difference 0.3 percentage points; virement £460,360 from risk budget
findings.quote: exceeding the budgeted 3% increase by 0.3 percentage points

findings.headline: HRA pension contribution rate cut from 23% to 16.5% has released £450,000, transferred to the HRA reserve to reduce borrowing
findings.detail: The paper proposes a temporary in-year virement of £450,000 from the HRA salary budget to the HRA reserve. The paper states this will reduce borrowing needed for capital projects this financial year and the HRA's ongoing borrowing costs.
findings.matters: A pension contribution change releasing cash into a reserve to reduce HRA borrowing is a funding decision a lender tracking HRA capital would note.
findings.figures: Employer pension contribution rate reduced from 23% to 16.5%; £450,000 released and transferred to HRA reserve; HRA underspend £605k
findings.quote: the reduction in the employer’s pension contribution rate from 23% to 16.5% has released £450,000.

findings.headline: Highways, Transport and Recycling moves from a £272k overspend reported at Quarter 1 to a £86k underspend at Quarter 2
findings.detail: The improvement reflects increased external grant use, improved income and continued expenditure management. The service still reports pressures in school transport, residual waste and fleet, and the forecast depends on delivery of a £1.4m savings programme.
findings.matters: A large service moving from overspend to underspend in one quarter, while still dependent on £1.4m of savings, is a recovery pattern peers would examine.
findings.figures: Q2 underspend £86k (against working budget £39,165k); Q1 overspend £272k; savings programme £1.4m
findings.quote: HTR now forecasting a £86k underspend compared with the £272k overspend

findings.headline: Schools' forecast deficits reduced by £127k compared with Quarter 1, with 23 schools projecting a deficit of £7.054 million
findings.detail: The paper reports 57 schools projecting a surplus of £3.914 million and 23 schools in deficit, giving a net position of £3.140 million deficit across 80 schools. Schools delegated budgets are forecast to overspend by £421k, and governing bodies' reserve draw has reduced from £0.358m to £0.019m.
findings.matters: A reduction in school deficits alongside a reducing draw on school reserves is a movement finance officers at other councils managing school budget pressures would compare against.
findings.figures: Schools deficits reduced by £127k; 23 schools in deficit totalling £7,054,132; 57 schools in surplus totalling £3,914,349; net £3,139,783 deficit; governing body reserve draw reduced from £0.358m to £0.019m
findings.quote: have reduced by £127k compared with quarter 1.

daily_post.headline: The Pensions Regulator's reporting breaches of the law area has two of four modules fully compliant, with one amber and one question in progress.
daily_post.lead: Open items on breaches reporting to the regulator are the kind of governance gap a finance director would track against peers, and the paper gives no completion date for them.
